comments.author: zovirl
comments.story_title: Ask HN: Recommend resources that helped your game dev journey?
comments.quote_zh: 真正让我深刻体会到打磨有多重要。
comments.text_zh: 帮我入门的一些资源：Brathwaite & Schreiber 的《Challenges for Games Designers》。这是迄今为止最有帮助的，因为它给出了一个寻找并打磨有趣的游戏创意的流程。Swink 的《Game Feel》。它考察了为什么 Super Mario 里的跳跃感觉比 Donkey Kong 更好、为什么 Street Fighter 的手感是那样，等等。这种拆解和审视机制的方式让我大开眼界，也可以应用到其他类型的游戏上。lostgarden.com，尤其是 [LINK]，它描述了一个快速迭代创意的流程；还有 [LINK]，它向我介绍了一些游戏机制的基本构建块。后来帮助我的资源：我发现《Art of Game Design》在后来很有帮助，当时我在努力把一款好游戏做成一款伟大的游戏。不同的透镜很适合用来找出我可以改进游戏的地方。[VIDEO] 真正让我深刻体会到打磨（polish）有多重要。这在我已经有了一款还算有点好玩的游戏之后很有用。最后，一个观察和一个建议，如果你愿意听的话：你承认自己不懂游戏设计，却试图通过移除限制来创新。这对初学者来说似乎是个巨大的挑战，就像一个人不会演奏乐器却试图创造一种新的爵士风格。我认为如果你先学会演奏这件乐器，会更成功：通过做大量小游戏来练习。每个花 2-4 天，不要更多。学会用原型来探索设计空间，寻找具备……的点子：
comments.text: Resources which helped me get started: "Challenges for Games Designers" by Brathwaite & Schreiber. This was by far the most helpful, as it laid out a process of finding & refining fun game ideas. "Game Feel" by Swink. Examines why jumping feels better in Super Mario than Donkey Kong, why Street Fighter feels the way it does, etc. This way of breaking down & examining mechanics was eye opening and can be applied to other kinds of games. lostgarden.com, especially [LINK] , which describes a process for rapidly iterating on ideas, and [LINK] , which introduced me to some of the fundamental building blocks of game mechanics. Resources which helped me later: I found "Art of Game Design" to be helpful later, when working on making a good game into a great game. The different lenses were great for finding areas where I could improve a game. [VIDEO] really drove home how important polish is. This was useful after I had a game which was already a bit fun. Finally, an observation & a suggestion, if you're open to them: You admit that you don't know game design, yet you're attempting to innovate by removing limits. This seems like an enormous challenge for a beginner, like someone who doesn't know how to play an instrument attempting to make a new style of jazz. I think you'd have more success if you learned to play the instrument first: Practice by making a lot of small games. Spend 2-4 days on each, no more. comments.author: tripzilch
comments.story_title: 2 Days Trying To Create a Multiplayer HTML5 Game
comments.text_zh: 读起来非常有意思！我想我之后也得找机会试试做多人 HTML5 游戏，因为光是读你的文章，我相信你，但同时又很难相信它会那么难 :) 能不能稍微展开说说你说的“把整个棋盘状态都传过去数据量太大”那部分？看你的游戏，我不觉得棋盘状态会超过 100 字节左右？是 JSON 把它撑大了吗？如果我是你，我会这么做：把状态拆成静态部分和动态部分。玩家的名字在游戏过程中不会变。或者如果会变，也许更好的做法是把状态拆成高延迟和低延迟两部分。玩家名字晚一秒更新没什么大不了，所以可以通过另一个更慢的通道来传。其他所有数据——棋盘状态、玩家位置、分数——如果你每次传的字段都一样，就不需要用 JSON。所以确保所有东西都是有范围的整数，然后把它们压在一起，可以用 base64 库，或者干脆用 Number.toString 和 ParseInt 以 36 为基数（这是 JS 原生支持的最大基数编码，仍然有 5.17 bits/byte），或者你也可以折腾 Unicode/UTF8，把整数码点转成字节再转回来（你大概应该选后者，因为那会很酷）。哦还有个小提示，你写到：> 我加了一些规则和玩法元素，让它更像人们会想玩的东西，包括：被击中时的反馈
comments.text: Very interesting to read! I guess I'll have to try my hand at multiplayer HTML5 game as well some time, because even reading you, I believe you, but at the same time it's hard to believe that it's hard like that :) Care to elaborate a bit on the part where you say communicating the entire board state was too much data? Looking at your game, I don't see how the board state could be much more than 100 bytes or so? Was it the JSON that bloated it up? If I were you, I'd do it like this: split the state into a static and dynamic part. Player's names won't change during the game. Or if they might, maybe even better to split the state into a high and low latency part. If you see a Player's name update a second too late, it's no big deal, so communicate that via a different, slower, channel. All the other data, the board state, player positions, scores, you don't need JSON if you're transmitting the same fields every time. So make sure everything's a ranged integer and squeeze them together either using a base64 library, or maybe just simply Number.toString and ParseInt with radix 36 (max natively supported radix encoding in JS, and still 5.17 bits/byte), or maybe you hack Unicode/UTF8 to translate integer code-points into bytes and vice versa (you should probably go for the latter, because it'll be awesome ). comments.text_zh: 我相信这个词最初来自游戏开发领域。Martin Jonasson 与 Petri Purho（Noita 和 Crayon Physics Deluxe 的创作者）在 2010 年做过一场著名演讲，Juice it or lose it：[VIDEO] 另一个关于同一主题的经典演讲来自 Jan Willem Nijman 在 2013 年的 The art of screenshake：[LINK] 很高兴看到这些术语被更广泛的软件开发行业采用，不过我怀疑我们短期内不会在网站或工具类应用上看到太多“屏幕震动”。
comments.text: I believe the term comes from the game development sphere originally. Martin Jonasson & Petri Purho (creator of Noita and Crayon Physics Deluxe ) gave a famous talk about it in 2010, Juice it or lose it : [VIDEO] Another classic talk on the same topic comes from Jan Willem Nijman in 2013, The art of screenshake : [LINK] It's nice to see these terms being adopted by the wider software development industry, though I doubt we'll be seeing much screenshake on websites or utility apps any time soon.

comments.text_zh: 相关。Syntax.fm 播客采访了 Wordle 的创作者[0]。他在里面谈到自己看过一个关于添加“juice”的演讲[1]，以及这如何影响了这款游戏的一些 UX 决策。我个人认为，对于 Wordle 这种涉及文本/阅读的网页游戏来说，它的 juice 用量恰到好处。我觉得给网站/应用加一点 juice 挺好，但它们不是游戏，我认为应该保持在最低限度。了解你的受众。我不希望我的任何金融相关应用充满不必要的 juice，但这并不意味着我在等待某些流程时不需要反馈。有时应用会试图用花哨的转场来显得酷/前卫，这些东西我头几次看到时觉得挺酷，但之后就变得烦人，因为我每次都得等它。总之我在东拉西扯，但你明白大意：不要过度使用 juice，而 juice 的程度取决于你的受众和产品性质。0. comments.text: Related. Syntax.fm podcast interviewed the creator of Wordle[0]. In it he talked about seeing a talk[1] about adding "juice" and how it influenced some of the UX decisions for the game. I personally think that Wordle had the perfect amount a juice for what it was, a web game that involved text/reading. I think it's nice to add some juice to website/apps but they are not games and I think should be kept at a minimum. Know your audience. I don't want any of my finance related apps full of unnecessary juice, but that doesn't mean I don't want feedback for any processes I'm waiting for. Sometimes apps try to be cool/edgy with fancy transitions and those things look cool the first few times I see it but get annoying after that because I'm having to wait for it every time. Anyways I am rambling but you get the gist, don't overuse juice and the level of juice depends on your audience and the nature of your product. 0. [LINK] 1. [VIDEO]
